## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
## inst/scripts/make-data.R
##
## The documentation below is based on publicly avaiable data on GEO
## and on intermediate files that are too large to distribute with the 
## package, so the script is NOT intended to be run end-to-end.
## It records what was done, from what
## source, with what tool, at what parameters, so that the files in
## inst/extdata/ can be traced back to their origin and regenerated by users
## with appropriate access.
##
## All example files cover a demonstration region on chromosome 2
## (chr2:171,900,000-172,700,000, hg38) in 10 pseudeo samples C42B MicroC
## data, which is downloaded from GSE205000.

## 1. Hi-C contact matrices: inst/extdata/example_hic/sample*.hic
##
## Source
## ------
## Paired-end Micro-C data of C42B cell line were
## obtained from GEO databse under the session ID GSE205000.
##
## Preprocessing
## -------------
## FASTQs were processed to per-sample .hic files following 4DN pipeline.
## Briefly, we first aligned the raw sequencing reads (i.e., fastq files) 
## with BWA MEM (v0.7.17), and the aligned reads were paired, sorted, and 
## filtered with Pairtools (v0.3.0) and converted into pairs files. Next, 
## we normalized paired data to generate matrix files with Juicertools 
## for Juicer (v1.5) (hic files).
##
## Pseudeo samples generation
## --------------------------
## 10 samples were generated by randomly plus and minus a randome value from
## 1-10 in the hic matrix on chr2. Then each hic matrix were subsetted to 
## chr2:172,207,000-172,457,000 to be used as the example data for loopQTL. 
##
## Sketch (bash + R, using hictk for format conversion):
##
##   # 1. Dump chr2 contact pixels at 5 kb from the full-size C42B .hic
##   hictk dump C42B_Micro_1_Billion.hic \
##       --resolution 5000 --range 2 --join \
##       > chr2_source_pixels.bg2
##
##   # 2. Per-sample perturbation in R: for each non-zero pixel, add
##   #    delta ~ Uniform({-10..-1, 1..10}) (never 0), clamp at 0.
##   #    Writes sample1.bg2 .. sample10.bg2 with chrom "2" -> "chr2".
##   #    Full script shipped at inst/scripts/generate_pseudo_hic.R.
##   Rscript inst/scripts/generate_pseudo_hic.R \
##       chr2_source_pixels.bg2 outdir/ 10 42
##
##   # 3. Load each perturbed BG2 back into a per-sample .hic file.
##   printf "chr2\t242193529\n" > chr2.chrom.sizes
##   for i in $(seq 1 10); do
##       hictk load -c chr2.chrom.sizes -b 5000 -f bg2 \
##           --output-fmt hic sample${i}.bg2 sample${i}.hic
##   done
##
##   # 4. Subset each .hic to the demo region chr2:171.9-172.7 Mb at 5 kb.
##   for i in $(seq 1 10); do
##       hictk dump sample${i}.hic --resolution 5000 \
##           --range chr2:171900000-172700000 --join > sub${i}.bg2
##       hictk load -c chr2.chrom.sizes -b 5000 -f bg2 \
##           --output-fmt hic sub${i}.bg2 \
##           inst/extdata/example_hic/sample${i}.hic
##   done


## =============================================================================
## 2. Loop calls: inst/extdata/example_loops/sample*_loops.bedpe
## =============================================================================
##
## Source and method
## -----------------
## Per-sample significant chromatin loops were called from the origianl C42B .hic
## file using FitHiC. Only long range loops (anchor distance > 30KB) with significance
## (q-value <= 0.05) were kept for the loopQTL analysis demo. The loops were randomly 
## selected and edited with following code.
##
## Sketch (bash):
##
##   # Per-sample loop perturbation in R: for each pseudo sample,
##   #   (1) drop a Uniform(5%, 10%) fraction of the source loops,
##   #   (2) shift 20% of what remains by +/- 1 bin (5 kb) on each
##   #       anchor independently.
##   # Writes sample1_loops.bedpe .. sample10_loops.bedpe.
##   # Full script shipped at inst/scripts/generate_pseudo_loops.R.
##   Rscript inst/scripts/generate_pseudo_loops.R \
##       C42B_Micro_1_Billion_FitHiC_q0.05_30KB-2Mb.bedpe \
##       chr2 outdir/ 10 5000 42
##
##   # Then subset each sample's BEDPE to the demo region.
##   for i in $(seq 1 10); do
##       awk 'BEGIN{s=171900000; e=172700000}
##            $1=="chr2" && $2>=s && $3<=e &&
##            $4=="chr2" && $5>=s && $6<=e' \
##           outdir/sample${i}_loops.bedpe \
##           > inst/extdata/example_loops/sample${i}_loops.bedpe
##   done


## =============================================================================
## 3. Genotypes: inst/extdata/example.vcf.gz (+ .tbi)
## =============================================================================
##
## A pseudeo genotype vcf was made following below code:
##
## Sketch (bash):
##
##   # Source: 54-sample WGS VCF matched to the public mCRPC Hi-C samples,
##   #         indexed with tabix (hg38 coordinates).
##   SRC=101mCRPC_fromWGS_HiC_4bed.vcf.gz
##
##   # 1. Pick the first 10 samples from the source header and map their
##   #    original IDs to sample1..sample10.
##   zcat $SRC | grep "^#CHROM" | cut -f10- | tr "\t" "\n" | head -n 10 \
##       | awk 'BEGIN{i=1} {print $0"\tsample"i; i++}' > rename.tsv
##   IDS=$(cut -f1 rename.tsv | paste -sd,)
##
##   # 2. Subset to chr2 and those 10 samples, then reheader with sample*
##   bcftools view -r chr2 -s $IDS $SRC -Ou \
##     | bcftools reheader -s rename.tsv \
##     | bcftools view -Oz -o chr2_pseudo_realGT.vcf.gz
##   tabix -p vcf chr2_pseudo_realGT.vcf.gz
##
##   # 3. Randomize genotypes: for each (SNP, sample), draw GT uniformly
##   #    from {0/0, 0/1, 1/1} so each SNP has ~33/33/33 proportions;
##   #    strip all other FORMAT fields so only GT remains.
##   zcat chr2_pseudo_realGT.vcf.gz \
##     | awk 'BEGIN { srand(42); gt[0]="0/0"; gt[1]="0/1"; gt[2]="1/1" }
##            /^#/ { print; next }
##            { printf "%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\tGT",
##                     $1,$2,$3,$4,$5,$6,$7,$8
##              for (i=10; i<=NF; i++) { r=int(rand()*3); printf "\t%s", gt[r] }
##              printf "\n" }' \
##     | bgzip -c > chr2_pseudo.vcf.gz
##   tabix -p vcf chr2_pseudo.vcf.gz
##
##   # 4. Subset to the demo region chr2:171.9-172.7 Mb
##   bcftools view -r chr2:171900000-172700000 chr2_pseudo.vcf.gz -Oz \
##       -o inst/extdata/example.vcf.gz
##   tabix -p vcf inst/extdata/example.vcf.gz

## =============================================================================
## 4. Gene annotation: inst/extdata/example.gtf.gz
## =============================================================================
##
## Source
## ------
## GENCODE Human basic annotation, release 29 (hg38).
##   https://www.gencodegenes.org/human/release_29.html
## File: gencode.v29.basic.annotation.gtf.gz
##
## Subsetting
## ----------
## Filtered to records on chr2 whose feature interval overlaps the demo
## region, keeping the original GENCODE two-line header:
##
##   zcat gencode.v29.basic.annotation.gtf.gz \
##     | awk 'BEGIN{OFS="\t"}
##            /^#/ {print; next}
##            $1=="chr2" && $4<=173500000 && $5>=171000000' \
##     | gzip > inst/extdata/example.gtf.gz


## =============================================================================
## 5. Regulatory peaks: inst/extdata/example_annotation.bed
## =============================================================================
##
## Source
## ------
## C42B IDR H3K27ac ChIP-seq peak set downloaded from ENCODE (ENCSR279KIX).
##
## Subsetting
## ----------
## Keep chr2 peaks only and drop everything past column 3 so that
## rtracklayer::import() reads a clean BED3 regardless of narrowPeak's
## non-integer score column.
##
##   awk '$1=="chr2" {print $1"\t"$2"\t"$3}' \
##       C42B_WT_H3K27ac.comb.optimal.final.filt.MACS2.narrowPeak \
##       > inst/extdata/example_annotation.bed

## =============================================================================
## 6. Samplesheet: inst/extdata/example_samplesheet.tsv
## =============================================================================
##
## A TSV file with matched ID to its per-sample .hic file,
## per-sample loops BEDPE. Format is documented in ?loopQTLsetup().
